questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Nefarious'.
questions.x: 'Nefarious' means wicked. 'Virtuous' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to: COVERT
questions.x: 'Covert' is the opposite of 'Overt'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Covert'.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To rest on one's laurels'
o: To be satisfied with past success and stop trying
To sleep on a bed of leaves
questions.x: 'To rest on one's laurels' means: to be satisfied with past success and stop trying.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: TREPIDATION
questions.x: 'Trepidation' means fear. 'Courage' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: The claim was rejected as it was not ____ by documents.
questions.x: Correct answer: supported. Passive voice needs the past participle.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Fortitude'.
questions.x: 'Fortitude' means courage. 'Cowardice' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To spill the beans'
questions.x: 'To spill the beans' means: to reveal secret information.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Notorious'.
questions.x: 'Notorious' is the opposite of 'Reputable'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Notorious'.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
If I was the Commissioner, / I would simplify / the claim forms.
questions.x: The error is in part (a): 'If I was the Commissioner'. Hypothetical condition takes 'were': 'If I were the Commissioner'.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Had I known / about the change in rules, / I would have informed you.
questions.x: The sentence is grammatically correct as written. Correct inverted third conditional.

questions.q: Why do many firms hesitate to train apprentices?
o: They fear trained apprentices will leave for competitors
questions.x: Answer: 'They fear trained apprentices will leave for competitors'. The passage states this concern. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Apprenticeships combine learning with earning. A young person who trains on the shop floor while receiving a stipend gains skills that classrooms alone cannot provide, and employers get workers trained to their needs. Yet many firms hesitate, worried that trained apprentices will leave for competitors. Shared training funds and recognised certificates can reduce this fear by spreading costs and making skills portable.

questions.q: What remedy does the author suggest?
o: Shared training funds and recognised certificates
questions.x: Answer: 'Shared training funds and recognised certificates'. These measures spread costs and make skills portable. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Apprenticeships combine learning with earning. A young person who trains on the shop floor while receiving a stipend gains skills that classrooms alone cannot provide, and employers get workers trained to their needs. Yet many firms hesitate, worried that trained apprentices will leave for competitors. Shared training funds and recognised certificates can reduce this fear by spreading costs and making skills portable.

questions.q:
In which year did the following take place?
Subhas Chandra Bose proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free India at Singapore.
questions.x: Subhas Chandra Bose proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free India at Singapore in 1943. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q: Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki attempted to kill which magistrate in 1908?
questions.x: Correct answer: Kingsford. Khudiram Bose was executed at 18; Prafulla Chaki shot himself.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India was set up in 1935 on the recommendations of the:
questions.x: The Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance (1926) recommended a central bank.

questions.q: Arrange the following in chronological order: 1. Cripps Mission 2. August Offer 3. Wavell Plan 4. Cabinet Mission
questions.x: August Offer (1940), Cripps Mission (1942), Wavell Plan (1945), Cabinet Mission (1946).

questions.q: The 1938 session of the Indian National Congress, presided over by Subhas Chandra Bose, was held at:
questions.x: It was held at Haripura; it was the session at which the National Planning Committee idea was taken up.

questions.q: The 'Individual Satyagraha' of 1940 began with which person as the first satyagrahi?
questions.x: Correct answer: Vinoba Bhave. Nehru was the second.

questions.q: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the appointment of the Simon Commission (1927)?
questions.x: Lord Irwin was Viceroy during the appointment of the Simon Commission (1927).

questions.q: The newspaper/journal 'Amrita Bazar Patrika' is associated with:
o: Barindra Kumar Ghosh and Bhupendranath Dutta
Sisir Kumar Ghosh and Motilal Ghosh
questions.x: 'Amrita Bazar Patrika' was started/edited by Sisir Kumar Ghosh and Motilal Ghosh.

questions.q: Who founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924)?
questions.x: The Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924) was founded by B. R. Ambedkar.

questions.q: Who among the following was a Moderate leader and the political guru of Gandhi?
questions.x: Correct answer: Gopal Krishna Gokhale. Gandhi regarded Gokhale as his political mentor.

questions.q: The military exercise 'Khanjar' is conducted between India and:
questions.x: 'Khanjar' is a bilateral exercise between India and Kyrgyzstan.

questions.q: The headquarters of the NATO is located in:
questions.x: NATO: headquartered in Brussels.

questions.q: National Doctors' Day (Dr. B. C. Roy) is observed on:
questions.x: National Doctors' Day (Dr. B. C. Roy): 1 July.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's G20 presidency:
1. The African Union was admitted as a permanent member.
2. The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched.
3. The summit failed to issue a leaders' declaration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The New Delhi Leaders' Declaration was adopted by consensus.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'social audit'?
o: Assessment of a public programme by its intended beneficiaries and community
questions.x: Correct answer: Assessment of a public programme by its intended beneficiaries and community. It is mandatory under MGNREGA.

questions.q: Which of the following organisations is headquartered in Gurugram?
questions.x: International Solar Alliance is based in Gurugram.

questions.q: The 'India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor' (IMEC) was announced at:
o: The G20 Summit in New Delhi, 2023
questions.x: It envisages rail and shipping links connecting India to Europe through the Gulf.

questions.q: 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' campaign launched on World Environment Day 2024 promotes:
o: Planting trees as a tribute to one's mother
questions.x: Correct answer: Planting trees as a tribute to one's mother. It is a mass tree-planting campaign.

questions.q: The 'Namo Bharat' trains, first operationalised in 2023, run on:
o: The Delhi–Ghaziabad–Meerut Regional Rapid Transit System
questions.x: Correct answer: The Delhi–Ghaziabad–Meerut Regional Rapid Transit System. They are India's first semi-high-speed regional trains.

questions.q: 'Operation Sindhu' (June 2025) involved evacuation of Indian nationals from:
questions.x: Correct answer: Iran and Israel. It was launched amid the Iran–Israel conflict.

questions.q: The practice of instant 'triple talaq' was held unconstitutional in:
o: Shayara Bano v. Union of India (2017)
questions.x: Parliament later enacted the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019.

questions.q: Who among the following was the first woman to become President of India?
questions.x: Pratibha Patil served 2007–2012; Droupadi Murmu (2022) is the first tribal woman President.

questions.q: The freeze on the number of Lok Sabha seats allotted to States, based on the 1971 census, has been extended until:
questions.x: Correct answer: The first census after 2026. The 84th Amendment (2001) extended the freeze.

questions.q: The Charter Act of 1833 is significant because it:
o: Made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India
Ended the East India Company's rule
questions.x: Correct answer: Made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India. Lord William Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment added Sindhi to the Eighth Schedule?
questions.x: It was the 21st Amendment Act of 1967.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
1. The Speaker continues in office even after the dissolution of the Lok Sabha until the new House meets.
2. The Speaker has a casting vote in case of a tie.
3. The Speaker is elected by the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Speaker is elected by the members of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: 'Cut motions' in Parliament are related to:
o: Demands for grants in the budget
questions.x: Correct answer: Demands for grants in the budget. Policy cut, economy cut and token cut motions seek to reduce demands.

questions.q: Article 12 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Definition of 'the State' for the purposes of Part III
Raising the level of nutrition and public health; prohibition of intoxicating drinks
questions.x: Article 12: Definition of 'the State' for the purposes of Part III.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Sessions of Parliament, prorogation and dissolution"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 85.

questions.q: Article 262 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights
Adjudication of disputes relating to waters of inter-State rivers
Protection of interests of minorities (language, script, culture)
questions.x: Article 262: Adjudication of disputes relating to waters of inter-State rivers.

questions.q:
Consider the following about GST:
1. GST subsumed central excise duty and service tax.
2. Petroleum crude is currently outside GST.
3. Alcohol for human consumption is under GST.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Alcohol for human consumption is constitutionally outside GST; five petroleum products are outside until the Council decides.

questions.q: 'Effective revenue deficit', a concept introduced in 2011–12, excludes from the revenue deficit:
o: Grants for creation of capital assets
questions.x: Such grants create durable assets even though booked as revenue expenditure.

questions.q: The 'multiplier' in Keynesian economics is equal to:
questions.x: Correct answer: 1 ÷ (1 − MPC). A higher marginal propensity to consume raises the multiplier.

questions.q: Which financial regulator oversees the National Pension System?
questions.x: PFRDA regulates NPS and APY.

questions.q: BRICS expanded in 2024 to include which of these countries?
o: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE
questions.x: Correct answer: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE. Indonesia joined as a full member in January 2025.

questions.q: The Bharatmala Pariyojana relates to:
questions.x: Correct answer: Highway development. Sagarmala relates to ports; UDAN to regional air connectivity.

questions.q: The 'Ease of Doing Business' report, discontinued in 2021, was published by the:
questions.x: Correct answer: World Bank. It was replaced by the 'Business Ready' (B-READY) project.

questions.q: The World Trade Organization came into existence on:
questions.x: Correct answer: 1 January 1995. It replaced GATT; its headquarters is in Geneva.

questions.q: Nominal GDP of a country is ₹2,36,250 crore and real GDP (at base-year prices) is ₹1,89,000 crore. The GDP deflator is:
questions.x:
GDP deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100 = (2,36,250 / 1,89,000) × 100 = 125.
Prices have risen 25% over the base year.

questions.q: Which committee/body is associated with "Economic capital framework of the RBI"?
questions.x: Bimal Jalan Committee (2019) dealt with economic capital framework of the rbi.

questions.q: On an inter-State supply of goods, the tax levied is:
questions.x: IGST is collected by the Centre and apportioned.

questions.q: Which inventory cost formula is NOT permitted under Ind AS 2?
questions.x: LIFO is not permitted under Ind AS 2 (and AS 2).

questions.q: P and Q share profits in the ratio 3 : 4. They admit R for a 1/6 share, which R acquires from P and Q in their existing ratio. The new profit-sharing ratio of P, Q and R is:
A partner withdrew ₹5,000 at the middle of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 9% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 5,000 = ₹60,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the middle of each month = 6 months.
Interest = 60,000 × 9% × 6/12 = ₹2,700.

questions.q: Government accounts are kept in three parts. Which of these is NOT one of them?
questions.x: The three parts are the Consolidated Fund (Art. 266), Contingency Fund (Art. 267) and Public Account (Art. 266(2)).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental accounting assumption under AS 1 (Disclosure of Accounting Policies)?
questions.x: AS 1 lists going concern, consistency and accrual as fundamental assumptions; prudence is a consideration in selecting policies.

questions.q: Goods returned by customers are recorded in the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Sales returns (returns inward) book. Returns inward reduce sales; a credit note is issued.

questions.q: The cash book of a firm shows a debit (bank) balance of ₹33,000. Cheques issued but not yet presented: ₹3,500; cheques deposited but not yet credited: ₹2,000; bank charges debited only in the pass book: ₹400; interest credited only in the pass book: ₹600. The balance as per the pass book is:
questions.x:
Start with cash book balance ₹33,000.
+ Cheques issued not presented (bank has not yet paid) 3,500
− Cheques deposited not credited 2,000
− Bank charges 400
+ Interest credited 600
Pass book balance = ₹34,700.

questions.q: Personal income tax of the proprietor paid out of business cash is debited to:
questions.x: The proprietor's income tax is a personal liability, so it is drawings.

questions.q: Under Schedule III, an asset expected to be realised within the company's normal operating cycle or within 12 months is classified as:
questions.x: Correct answer: Current asset. Classification follows the operating cycle or 12-month criterion.

questions.q: From the following, compute Gross Profit: Opening stock ₹55,000; Purchases ₹3,00,000; Purchase returns ₹2,000; Carriage inwards ₹3,000; Sales ₹4,03,500; Sales returns ₹2,000; Closing stock ₹10,000.
questions.x:
Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Purchase returns + Carriage inwards − Closing stock
= 55,000 + 3,00,000 − 2,000 + 3,000 − 10,000 = ₹3,46,000.
Gross profit = Net sales − COGS = 4,03,500 − 2,000 − 3,46,000 = ₹55,500.
Carriage inwards is a direct expense (Trading A/c).

questions.q: Opening inventory is ₹70,000, closing inventory is ₹70,000 and cost of goods sold for the year is ₹3,50,000. The inventory turnover ratio is:
questions.x:
Average inventory = (70,000 + 70,000) / 2 = ₹70,000.
Inventory turnover = COGS / Average inventory = 3,50,000 / 70,000 = 5 times.

questions.q: Fixed costs are ₹1,10,000; selling price ₹60 and variable cost ₹35 per unit. How many units must be sold to earn a profit of ₹17,500?
questions.x:
Required units = (Fixed cost + Target profit) / Contribution per unit
= (1,10,000 + 17,500) / 25 = 5,100 units.

questions.q: Purchases during a month: 1st — 200 units @ ₹15; 10th — 150 units @ ₹18; 20th — 150 units @ ₹22. 400 units were issued on the 25th. Value of closing stock under FIFO is:
questions.x: Under FIFO the earliest units are issued first, so the 100 units left come from the latest purchases: 100 × ₹22 = ₹2,200.

questions.q: Under the Code on Social Security, employment exchanges are renamed as:
questions.x: Employers must report vacancies to Career Centres before filling them (the Employment Exchanges Act, 1959 was subsumed).

questions.q: Under industrial relations theory, the 'unitary' perspective views the organisation as:
o: A team with common goals where conflict is abnormal
A coalition of competing interest groups
questions.x: The unitary frame assumes harmony and sees unions as unnecessary; pluralist and radical frames differ.

questions.q: Under the Code on Wages, for an employee whose minimum wage is fixed on an hourly or daily basis, a 'normal working day' is ordinarily fixed by the appropriate government at:
o: Any length decided by the employer
Up to the hours prescribed (commonly 8 hours), with weekly rest
questions.x: The appropriate government fixes the normal working day and weekly rest; overtime beyond that attracts double rate.

questions.q: In Excel Wear v. Union of India (1978), the Supreme Court struck down the then Section 25-O of the Industrial Disputes Act because:
o: The unfettered requirement of permission for closure was an unreasonable restriction on the right to carry on business
It applied only to public sector units
It violated the right to strike
questions.x: The Court held that the right to close a business is part of Article 19(1)(g); Section 25-O was later re-enacted with safeguards.

questions.q: Within how many days of retrenchment must the amount from the Worker Re-skilling Fund be credited to the retrenched worker's account?
questions.x: The amount (15 days' wages) is to be transferred to the worker's account within 45 days of retrenchment, to be used for upskilling.

questions.q: Taylor's differential piece-rate system pays:
o: The same rate to all workers
A higher rate to workers who reach the standard output and a lower rate to those who do not
questions.x: F. W. Taylor's scheme rewarded efficient workers with a higher piece rate.

questions.q: In 2022 the ILO added 'a safe and healthy working environment' to its fundamental principles. Which two conventions consequently became fundamental conventions?
questions.x: The 110th ILC (2022) made OSH a fundamental principle; C155 (OSH, 1981) and C187 (Promotional Framework for OSH, 2006) became fundamental, taking the total to ten.

questions.q: Workers of a company with 2,500 workers apply for registration of a union. The minimum membership required under the IR Code is:
questions.x: 10% of 2,500 = 250, but the rule takes 10% or 100 workers, whichever is less — so 100.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The OSH Code raised the threshold for applicability of contract labour provisions from 20 to 50 workers.
Reason (R): The Code abolished the principal employer's responsibility for welfare facilities to contract workers.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true but R is false. A is correct. R is false: the principal employer remains responsible for welfare facilities (drinking water, toilets, first-aid) for contract labour.

questions.q: In Air India v. Nergesh Meerza (1981), the Supreme Court struck down service rules that terminated air hostesses on:
questions.x: Termination on first pregnancy was held arbitrary and abhorrent; retirement on marriage within four years was upheld at the time.

questions.q: The Employees' Provident Fund Appellate Tribunal (EPFAT), which heard appeals against EPFO orders, was merged in 2017 with the:
questions.x: The Finance Act, 2017 merged EPFAT with CGIT, which now hears appeals under the EPF Act (and the Code on Social Security).

questions.q: In which year was the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act enacted?
questions.x: The Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act was enacted in 1996.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): A strike in breach of the notice provisions of the IR Code is illegal.
Reason (R): Workers participating in an illegal strike are not entitled to wages for the strike period and may face penalties.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both statements are true. But R describes consequences of an illegal strike; it does not explain why the strike is illegal (that follows from breach of statutory notice requirements).

questions.q: Which ground for disqualification from bonus was newly added in the Code on Wages (it was not in the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965)?
o: Riotous or violent behaviour on the premises
questions.x: The Code adds conviction for sexual harassment as a ground for disqualification alongside fraud, violent behaviour, theft, misappropriation and sabotage.

questions.q: Under the IR Code, 'last come, first go' is the principle followed in:
questions.x: Retrenchment ordinarily follows seniority within the category — the worker employed last is retrenched first — unless reasons are recorded.

questions.q: An employee leaves service after 4 years and 8 months as a regular (not fixed-term) employee on resignation. Under the gratuity provisions:
o: The employee is not entitled to gratuity as five years of continuous service are not completed (courts have, however, debated the 240-day rule in the fifth year)
The employer must pay double gratuity
The employee gets pro-rata gratuity like a fixed-term employee
The employee is entitled to gratuity for 5 years
questions.x: Five years' continuous service is required on resignation; the one-year rule applies to fixed-term employees. Some High Courts count 240 days in the final year, but the statutory rule remains five years.

questions.q: An employer with 25 employees, each earning ₹14,000 (basic + DA), must pay monthly to EPFO (employer share + EDLI + admin charges at 0.5%):
The Annapurna scheme under NSAP provides eligible senior citizens with:
o: 10 kg of foodgrains per month free
questions.x: Annapurna gives 10 kg of foodgrains per month to eligible elderly not receiving old-age pension.

questions.q: Which benefit under ESI is payable for permanent disablement due to employment injury?
o: Monthly cash payment based on the loss of earning capacity, for life
questions.x: Permanent disablement benefit is paid monthly, proportionate to the loss of earning capacity certified by a Medical Board.

questions.q: The withdrawal benefit for an EPS member with less than 10 years of service is computed using:
o: Table D of the scheme, applied to wages at exit and years of service
questions.x: Correct answer: Table D of the scheme, applied to wages at exit and years of service. Table D gives multiples of salary based on years of service.

questions.q: TDS is deducted on EPF withdrawal if the member has less than five years of continuous service and the amount is at least:
questions.x: Section 192A of the Income Tax Act: TDS at 10% (with PAN) on withdrawals of ₹50,000 or more before five years.

questions.q: Who can be an 'Authorised Signatory' for an establishment on the EPFO employer portal?
o: A person authorised by the employer with digital signature/e-sign registered with EPFO
questions.x: Authorised signatories approve KYC and transfers using DSC or Aadhaar e-sign.

questions.q: An employee whose average daily wage is ₹171 works in an ESI-covered factory and earns ₹19,500 in a month. Which statement about the month's contribution is correct?
o: Only the employer pays 3.25% (≈ ₹634); the employee's share is exempt
Neither pays, as low-wage employees are excluded from coverage
questions.x: Employees whose average daily wage is up to ₹176 are exempt from paying their own 0.75% share, but they remain covered and the employer must still pay 3.25% of wages. Here employer share ≈ ₹634.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of 'universal' (categorical) social security benefits?
o: They are paid to all persons in a category (e.g., all elderly) regardless of income
They are paid only to employees
questions.x: Correct answer: They are paid to all persons in a category (e.g., all elderly) regardless of income. Universal benefits avoid exclusion errors but cost more.

questions.q: The claim form for EDLI benefit on the death of an EPF member is:
questions.x: Form 5IF is filed by the nominee/legal heirs; Form 13 is for transfer, Form 2 for nomination.

questions.q: On the death of an APY subscriber after 60, the spouse receives the same pension, and on the death of both, the nominee receives:
o: The pension wealth accumulated till age 60
questions.x: Correct answer: The pension wealth accumulated till age 60. The corpus accumulated till 60 is returned to the nominee.

questions.q: An eligible employee earns ₹20,000 per month. The notified minimum wage for the employment is ₹9,500 per month. If the establishment declares bonus at 20%, the annual bonus payable is (statutory computation):
questions.x:
For computing bonus, salary is capped at ₹7,000 or the minimum wage, whichever is higher: max(7,000, 9,500) = ₹9,500.
Salary for computation = min(20,000, 9,500) = ₹9,500.
Annual bonus = 9,500 × 12 × 20% = ₹22,800. Bonus must lie between 8.33% and 20%.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of EPFO?
questions.x: NPS is regulated by PFRDA; EPFO administers the EPF, EPS and EDLI schemes and SSAs.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Copper wires are used in household electrical wiring.
Reason (R): Copper has very low electrical resistivity and is ductile.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains why copper is chosen.

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure purity (density) of milk?
questions.x: Lactometer measures purity (density) of milk.

questions.q: A solar water heater's panels are usually painted black because black surfaces:
questions.x: Correct answer: Absorb more heat radiation. Good absorbers are also good emitters.

questions.q: The 'Henry' is the SI unit of:
questions.x: Henry measures inductance.

questions.q: Ultrasound is used in medical imaging because it:
o: Has frequency above the human audible range and reflects from tissue boundaries
questions.x: Correct answer: Has frequency above the human audible range and reflects from tissue boundaries. Humans hear roughly 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

questions.q: Which logic gate outputs 1 only when all its inputs are 1?
questions.x: NAND and NOR are universal gates.

questions.q: 'Virtual memory' allows a computer to:
o: Use part of the storage drive as an extension of RAM
questions.x: Correct answer: Use part of the storage drive as an extension of RAM. It is slower than physical RAM.

questions.q: The causative agent of chikungunya is:
o: Chikungunya virus (an alphavirus spread by Aedes mosquitoes)
questions.x: Chikungunya: Chikungunya virus (an alphavirus spread by Aedes mosquitoes).

questions.q: 5G mobile technology offers, compared with 4G:
o: Higher speeds and much lower latency
questions.x: Correct answer: Higher speeds and much lower latency. 5G services were launched in India in October 2022.

questions.q: In computing, 'SQL' stands for:
o: Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart
questions.x: SQL = Structured Query Language.

questions.q: LPG used as cooking gas is mainly a mixture of:
questions.x: Correct answer: Butane and propane. Ethyl mercaptan is added to give a smell for leak detection.

questions.q: Bt cotton is genetically modified to resist:
questions.x: Correct answer: Bollworm pests. A gene from Bacillus thuringiensis produces an insecticidal protein.

questions.q:
Members enrolled in a district (thousand) — 2018: 175  |  2019: 155  |  2020: 135  |  2021: 175  |  2022: 230.
In which year was the percentage growth over the previous year the highest?
questions.x:
Year-on-year growth: 2019: -11.43%; 2020: -12.9%; 2021: 29.63%; 2022: 31.43%.
Highest growth: 2022 (31.43%). Note: the largest absolute rise need not be the largest percentage rise.

questions.q: At simple interest a sum doubles itself in 16 years. In how many years will it become 5 times itself at the same rate?
questions.x:
Doubling means interest = 1 × principal in 16 years, i.e. rate = 100/16 = 6.25% p.a.
To become 5 times, interest must be 4 × principal.
Time = (4 × 100) / 6.25 = 64 years. (Rule: time ∝ number of times the principal is earned as interest.)

questions.q: Two trains of lengths 250 m and 260 m run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 36 km/h and 72 km/h. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
questions.x:
Opposite directions → relative speed = 36 + 72 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s.
Distance = sum of lengths = 510 m.
Time = 510 / 30 = 17 s.

questions.q: How many arrangements of the letters of 'TREASURY' are there in which the vowels are NOT all together?
questions.x:
Total arrangements = 20,160 (R appears 2 times).
Vowels together = 360 × 6 = 2,160.
Not all together = 20,160 − 2,160 = 18,000.

questions.q: A bag has 8 white and 8 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random together. What is the probability that at least one of them is white?
questions.x:
P(at least one white) = 1 − P(both black).
P(both black) = C(8,2)/C(16,2) = 28/120.
Required = 1 − 7/30 = 23/30.

questions.q: On which day of the week did 23 August 1988 fall?
questions.x:
Odd-day method (Sunday = 0).
Completed years = 1987: 1600 years → 0 odd days; 300 years → 1; remaining 87 years have 21 leap + 66 ordinary → 21×2 + 66 = 108 → 3 odd day(s).
Days elapsed in 1988 up to 23 August = 236 → 5 odd day(s).
Total = 1 + 3 + 5 = 9 → 2 → Tuesday.

questions.q: The monthly salary of a clerk rises by 25%, then falls by 25%, and finally rises by 20%. The overall percentage change is:
questions.x:
Multiply the growth factors: (1 + 25/100) × (1 − 25/100) × (1 + 20/100) = 1.25 × 0.75 × 1.2 = 1.125.
Overall change = (1.125 − 1) × 100 = 12.5% → 12.5% increase.
Note: simply adding (25 − 25 + 20) is wrong because each change acts on a new base.

questions.q: The average of 11 observations is 54. The average of the first 6 is 44 and that of the last 6 is 59. The 6th observation is:
questions.x:
Sum of all 11 = 11 × 54 = 594.
First 6 + last 6 = 6×44 + 6×59 = 618; the middle observation is counted twice.
Middle = 618 − 594 = 24.

questions.q: At what time between 9 and 10 o'clock will the hands of a clock point in opposite directions (be in a straight line but opposite)?
questions.x:
At 9:00 the minute hand is 45 minute-spaces behind the hour hand.
To be opposite it must gain 45 − 30 = 15 spaces; it gains 55 spaces in 60 minutes.
Time = 15 × 60/55 = 180/11 minutes = 16 4/11 minutes past 9.

questions.q: A starts a business with ₹30,000. B joins after 6 months with ₹20,000, and C joins after 7 months with ₹50,000. Out of a year-end profit of ₹43,800, B's share is:
questions.x:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time.
A: 30,000×12, B: 20,000×6, C: 50,000×5 → 36 : 12 : 25.
B's share = 12/73 × 43,800 = ₹7,200.

questions.q: The monthly incomes of P and Q are in the ratio 9 : 5 and their monthly expenditures are in the ratio 2 : 1. If each of them saves ₹2,000 a month, P's monthly income is:
questions.x:
Let incomes = 9k, 5k and expenditures = 2m, 1m.
9k − 2m = 5k − 1m = 2,000 → 4k = 1m.
Solving gives k = 2,000, m = 8,000.
P's income = 9 × 2,000 = ₹18,000 (check: ₹18,000 − ₹16,000 = ₹2,000).

questions.q: Find the greatest number that will divide 97, 209, 265 leaving the same remainder in each case.
questions.x:
If N leaves the same remainder, N divides the differences.
Differences: 209 − 97 = 112, 265 − 209 = 56.
HCF(112, 56) = 56.

questions.q: In a certain code language, QUOTA is written as UQSPE. How is PENCIL written in that code?
questions.x:
Compare QUOTA → UQSPE: Q→U, U→Q, O→S…
Rule: letters in odd positions move 4 forward and letters in even positions move 4 backward.
Applying it to PENCIL gives TARYMH.

questions.q: The mean of 7 observations is 64. If 6 of them are 50, 87, 82, 25, 56, 48, the remaining observation is:
questions.x:
Total = 7 × 64 = 448. Sum of known values = 348.
Missing = 448 − 348 = 100.
